## Answer: 8

I could not verify the link structure directly, so this relies on an invariant argument and leaves a symmetry ambiguity in the bidegree.

**1. Intermediate Jacobian.** The genus 9 prime Fano threefold X has $h^{1,2}(X)=3$, so $\dim J(X)=3$. Blowing up rational curves (lines) does not change $J$, so $\dim J(Y)=3$ for $Y=\mathrm{Bl}_{Z_1\sqcup Z_2}X$. I am assuming, as in the standard theory of Sarkisov links, that $J$ is preserved along the link to the conic bundle $V\to\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$, so $\dim J(V)=3$.

**2. Conic bundle Jacobian.** For a standard conic bundle $V\to S$ with $S=\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ (so $g(S)=0$), $\dim J(V)=g(\tilde\Delta)$, where $\tilde\Delta\to\Delta$ is the étale double cover of the discriminant curve $\Delta$. Hence $g(\tilde\Delta)=3$.

**3. Genus of the discriminant.** An étale double cover satisfies $p_a(\tilde\Delta)=2p_a(\Delta)-1$. Setting this equal to 3 gives $p_a(\Delta)=2$.

**4. Bidegree.** For a curve of bidegree $(a,b)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$, $p_a=(a-1)(b-1)$. So $(a-1)(b-1)=2$, which gives $(a,b)=(2,3)$ or $(3,2)$. The two options differ by the symmetry swapping the factors, and I cannot fix the convention from the given data. Taking the usual ordering $(a,b)=(2,3)$:

$$a^b = 2^3 = 8.$$

(The other ordering would give $3^2=9$.)

ANSWER: 8
